assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing all splitting rules.
Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Fulfillment/address: 6 rows covering grouping, splitting by address, splitting by type, pickup grouping, and mixed cases. Availability: 6 rows. Warehouse: 4 rows. Companion: 3 rows. Total 19 rows, no cross-multiplication.

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items with different fulfillment types (store pickup vs home delivery) cannot share a shipment.
assertions.evidence: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress includes row 'Delivery and pickup items always split' with camera (DELIVERY) and mug (PICKUP) in separate shipments

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items going to different addresses must be in separate shipments.
assertions.evidence: splitsShipmentsByFulfillmentTypeAndAddress includes row 'Same type, different delivery addresses' with camera (Addr-A) and watch (Addr-B) in separate shipments

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — in-stock items ship immediately, backordered/pre-ordered items ship when available.
assertions.evidence: splitsShipmentsByStockAvailability with 6 rows including 'In-stock item not held for a backordered item' showing IMMEDIATE and WHEN_AVAILABLE shipments separately

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation (minimising shipments) is represented as its own @TableTest — choosing which warehouses to ship from to minimise total shipment count.
assertions.evidence: choosesWarehouseCombinationMinimizingShipmentCount with 4 rows including 'Correct warehouse pair must be found, not just any pair' proving minimal-cover logic

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest — paired items (e.g. camera body and lens) should ship together from the same location when possible.
assertions.evidence: keepsCompanionProductsTogetherWhenPossible with 3 rows: tie-breaker, split when unavoidable, already together

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method includes all output columns for its concern in the same table — e.g. warehouse allocation includes both the assignment and shipment count, not split across methods. All outputs of the same concern belong together.
assertions.evidence: Each @TableTest has a single 'Shipments?' output column. Warehouse table includes W1/W2/W3 stock columns and Shipments? together. Companion table includes Companions and Shipments? together.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Shipments?', 'Groups?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Shipments?, Shipments?, Shipments?, Shipments?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation (e.g. 'Consolidate: two beats three', 'Everything at one warehouse') — not 'Test case 2'.
assertions.evidence: Scenarios named: 'Same fulfillment type and address', 'In-stock item not held for a backordered item', 'Correct warehouse pair must be found, not just any pair', 'Companions win a tie between equally minimal warehouses'

assertions.text: Column names use business/domain language (e.g. 'Shipments?' not 'Result?', 'Warehouse stock' not 'inventory_map'). The tables read as a specification a product person could review.
assertions.evidence: Columns: 'Scenario', 'Items', 'Shipments?', 'W1 Stock', 'W2 Stock', 'W3 Stock', 'Companions' — all domain language with '?' suffix on output columns

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
